answer_1.quote: Inspired by grammar rules proposed in the NLG literature (Rajkumar and White, 2014), ungrammatical variants were automatically filtered out by detecting dependency relation sequences not attested in the original HUTB corpus.
answer_1.outputs: The paper generates meaning-equivalent grammatical variants of reference sentences by permuting preverbal constituents and evaluates which ordering is preferred based on cognitive and discourse factors.

answer_2.quote: We set up a binary classification task to separate the original HUTB reference sentences from the variants using the cognitive metrics described in Section 2.

answer_4.quote: we conducted a targeted human evaluation via forced-choice rating task and collected sentence judgments from 12 Hindi native speakers for 167 randomly selected reference-variant pairs in our data set.
answer_4.guideline: Participants were first shown the preceding sentence, and then they were asked to select the best continuation between either the reference or the variant.
